studies.Reference: Carcinogenic air pollutants and breast cancer risk in the Arkansas rural community health study: A nested case-control study.
studies.Authors: Ellis ET, Young SG, Carroll R, Stahr SD, Runnells GA, Grasmuck EA, Su LJ, Park YM, Hsu PC
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Twelve census-tract level HAPs from the 2005 National Air Toxics Assessment were geocoded to participants' baseline addresses and categorized into tertiles.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 574 cases and 2295 incidence density-sampled controls matched 1:4 on index age and race
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: significantly increased risk of BC for ... high chromium
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: associations between carcinogenic HAPs and BC risk in a rural population
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: high chromium (OR_T3 = 1.31; 95% CI 1.00-1.70, P trend = 0.04); census-tract level HAPs from the 2005 National Air Toxics Assessment

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.9878). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 3 studies yielded an overall effect size of 1.13 (95% CI: 1.06–1.21), suggesting that chromium is associated with a higher risk of breast cancer. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.
